intent: Baseline symmetric 5-sensor array with 12 mm footprints, 10 mm spacing, 4 cm forward of the axle, to establish how a centred line-sensing layout performs before any geometry is varied. Next iterations will adjust sensor forward offset and spacing according to integration feedback and race telemetry.
learning: No prior evidence yet. Hypotheses to test: (1) 12 mm footprints with 10 mm spacing give a smooth signal across the tape; (2) a 4 cm forward sensor offset reduces rms_error on bends compared with sensors at the axle; (3) the 0.12 m wheel track is wide enough that turn rate does not saturate on the slalom. Ask the Integrator whether the signal is noisy or saturates at the outer sensors, and whether the robot loses the line on tight bends.
rationale: This is iteration 0 with no race data or integration feedback yet, so the design rests on the simulator contract alone. A 5-sensor line array gives a usable centroid across a 25 mm tape: with 12 mm footprints and 10 mm spacing, the outer sensors still see the tape when the robot drifts about 2 cm, and the centre sensors resolve small offsets. The sensors sit 4 cm ahead of the axle, so the controller reads the line before the wheels reach it, which should help on bends. The wheel track of 0.12 m and wheel radius of 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and enough ground speed to cover roughly 4.5 m in under 3 s with a typical base speed. Mass 0.8 kg and body length 0.18 m keep yaw inertia moderate, so steering responds without much overshoot. Body width 0.12 m raises the off-track limit to about 0.06 m, which is the floor and matches the 12 mm footprint and track half-width. I expect this to complete the development tracks at moderate speed, with the main uncertainty being whether the 4 cm lookahead causes oscillation on tight slalom bends.
